## Theme

<!-- parity: /theme -->

The TUI palette is data, never code. `/theme` lists every available theme
(built-ins first, then user themes) with a swatch preview; `/theme <name>`
switches immediately and persists the choice; `/theme reset` returns to
the default.

Config equivalent — the persisted theme name:

```yaml
tui:
  theme: default   # a built-in name or a user theme file stem
```

Built-in names: `default` (the historical site palette — teal `#5eead4`,
indigo `#818cf8`), `catppuccin`, `nord`, `dracula`, `ohmypi-dark`,
`ohmypi-light`, `pi`.

User themes live in `~/.fah/themes/<name>.json`; the file stem is the
theme name, and a user theme can never shadow a built-in (a clashing file
name is skipped with a boot note). The JSON holds a `"roles"` object mapping ROLE names to hex colors
(`"#rgb"` or `"#rrggbb"`): `accent`, `accent2`, `muted`, `highlight`,
`success`, `warning`, `error`, `border`, `focusBorder`, `userMessageBg`.
Every role is optional — a missing role inherits the default theme for
that slot. Unknown role names, invalid hex, or broken JSON produce a
named error (file, role, line) at load time, never a crash.

Applies: `/theme <name>` switches the live session in one frame; a direct
YAML edit takes effect at next boot. Asked to create a theme from a
description, write the JSON file, then apply it with `/theme <name>` and
confirm the swatch line with the user. Asked for a palette "like X" where
X is unknown, ask two or three palette questions first — never invent one
silently.

### Compaction report detail

By default an auto-compaction fold prints ONE short marker line
(`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the internal
checkpoint summary stays in the session file (reachable via
`compact_expand`) and out of the console. To render the full report block
(records + fenced summary) and the live summarizer stream on headless
runs, opt in:

```yaml
tui:
  showCompactionDetails: true
```

The manual `/compact` command always renders the full block. Applies at
next boot.

## Prompts, TTSR & A2A

The remaining user-file sections (all global scope):

```yaml
prompts:                        # prompt overrides: prompt id → text or @file
  concise: "Answer in one short paragraph."
ttsr:                           # tool-schema reduction (TTSR)
  enabled: true
  contextMode: keep             # keep | discard
  repeatMode: after-gap         # after-gap | once
a2a:                            # remote Agent2Agent endpoints
  servers:
    peer:
      url: https://peer.example:8080
      token: [REDACTED:Sensitive-Value]}      # env-resolved at boot — never a literal secret
fabric:                         # host discovery announcements (read-only:
  capabilities:                 # written by hosts, never user-edited)
    - name: yoclip.render
      description: Render the open project to MP4
```

`a2a` servers are remote-only (a `url`, like remote MCP servers), so they
configure fine on process-less hosts. A `token` is an `\${ENV}` reference
resolved at boot; config `check`/`set` keep the token text literal, so an
unset variable surfaces when the agent boots, not as a config error.

<!-- parity: /settings -->

## Example invocations

- `point project memory at ./memory` → Memory section: `config` op `set`,
  key `memory.projectPath`, value `./memory` (project file is the default

Console-output behavior flags (gh-1198 + gh-1433), user file. Today one

`streamThinking: true` (or the `--stream-thinking` flag, which wins for

flags needed). `--no-stream-thinking` silences thinking for one headless
run (the reasoning liveness line returns), and `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy`
reverts the whole headless face to the pre-gh-1433 byte shape for edge
hosts that parse the log. Rendered deltas — thinking AND streamed text,
on every face — pass through the redaction pipeline at render time since


## Tool-result & user-message spilling

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

Oversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and
the session keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678).
An oversized USER message (headless prompt, TUI input, steering) spills
to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/user-<n>.md` and the model receives a
bounded head+tail preview plus a read-in-parts instruction (issue
#1760). Tolerant parse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as
`[spills]` notes at boot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` = legacy
behavior (nothing spills — it beats the `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` /
`FAH_USER_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knobs too); `threshold: 0` disables
tool-result spilling only, `userThreshold: 0` the user path only:

```yaml
spills:
  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy
  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills; 0 = tools off
  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)
  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)
  userThreshold: 16384 # absolute byte floor for the user path; 0 = user off
  userFraction: 0.5 # spill a user message over this fraction of the live window budget
```

Applies at next boot.

## Session retention

<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->

The `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for
the sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a
boot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live
sessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than
`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all
nothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant
parse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. Run
`fa session clean [--dry-run]` to enforce the policy manually;
`sweep: off` makes the manual verb the only enforcement path:

```yaml
sessions:
  retention:
    maxTotalBytes: 5368709120 # total cap in bytes (0 = no cap, default)
    minAgeDays: 14 # never delete sessions used more recently than this
    keepNamed: true # named sessions (fa --session <name>) are exempt
    sweep: boot # boot (sweep at startup) | off (manual `fa session clean` only)
```

Applies at next boot (the sweep runs before the session opens).

## Project context budget

<!-- parity: notices on both surfaces; the byte knob is a config-file setting -->

`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md`/`GOAL.md`/`DESIGN.md` + Copilot
instruction files merge into the system prompt under a byte budget,
allocated leaf-first (deeper files win, issue #1761). Truncation is never
silent: the model sees a head excerpt plus an explicit
read-the-full-file instruction, a dropped file leaves a one-line
tombstone, and the user gets a boot notice per truncated/dropped file.
Tolerant parse: unknown keys surface as `[projectContext]` notes at boot,
never boot failures. `maxBytes: 0` disables the section entirely (no file

```yaml
projectContext:

```

<!-- parity: none (config-only surface; web/macOS app banner reads it too) -->

The `links:` section (issue #691) is the single source of truth for
product/store links — the App Store banner in the web/macOS apps, the
CLI, and the fa1.dev site generator all resolve the same values, so a
link changes in ONE place. Defaults are baked in; only overrides are
written. Strict parse: a non-map section, a non-URL value, or a

`play:` (the Google Play release) stays ABSENT until the Android release
is live — every surface renders the Android slot as "coming soon" while

`banner: false` is the regression switch: the Get surface stays
byte-identical to the legacy UI. The section is user-file only (like
`tui:`/`fabric:`) and applies at next boot for the in-app banner; the

## Auto update

<!-- parity: /update, settings hub -->

User file top-level key (issue #1377). The self-update policy — a
tri-state, because the honest default is neither silent-off nor
unattended-on:

```yaml
auto_update: true # true | false | "notify" (default notify)
```

`notify` (the default) checks the release feed once at boot and prints
when a newer version exists — nothing is downloaded. `true` is the
unattended arm: at boot a newer release is downloaded, provenance
verified and installed, and the session restarts onto the new binary.
`false` touches no update host at all. An absent key and an explicit
`"notify"` are the same policy — the default is never written. Strict
parse: anything but `true`, `false` or `"notify"` is a
`ConfigException`. Applies at next boot. `/update` runs a check-and-apply
immediately regardless of the policy; the settings hub exposes the same
tri-state.

## Design

### Problem
`persistConfig` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart` calls `saveCliConfig(home, saved.copyWith(...))` — a global-file write of the whole config, where sections the process didn't touch still render from the boot-loaded `saved` snapshot. With multiple concurrent REPLs, the last saver reverts other processes' edits (except customProviders, which merges; and sections in `_diskPreservedSections` where the emitter omitted them... but the emitter does NOT omit them — `saved` carries them, so caller-wins re-renders stale values).

Wait — actually let me re-check: `_preserveDiskSections` only re-attaches disk blocks the EMITTER OMITED. The boot's persistConfig carries `saved` (the boot snapshot) as copyWith base, so every section the boot loaded is rendered — stale values overwrite disk changes. That's the bug.

### Fix plan (per ticket)

1. **Three-way merge on save**: `saveCliConfig(homeDir, config, base: baseline)` — when `base` is provided, compare per-top-level-key rendered blocks: keys where `config`'s render == `base`'s render were NOT changed by this process → drop them from the emitted yaml so `_preserveDiskSections` re-attaches the current disk blocks (or leaves them absent when the disk no longer has them). Keys that differ → this process changed them → caller wins.

  Implementation detail: the comparison is string-level on top-level blocks of `base.toYaml()` vs `config.toYaml()`. Since both renders come from the same emitter, a per-key block equality is a faithful "unchanged" signal.

  Wait, subtle issue: `toYaml()` on base may render sections the current doesn't (e.g. `models:` where the live instance replaced it) — the per-key comparison still works: for each key in the CURRENT render, if the baseline render has an identical block → unchanged → drop from current emit. If baseline render's block differs or the key is absent in baseline → changed (or new) → keep.

  But there's a wrinkle: the boot renders `saved.toYaml()` — hmm, wait, actually there's a subtlety with `mode:` etc: The boot persistConfig sets `mode: cli.currentMode.name` which may equal `saved.mode` (unchanged) or differ (user switched `/mode`). Comparison handles that fine.

  Another subtlety: the baseline render must be computed ONCE at boot (or on each save from the CURRENT `saved` snapshot?). Hmm. In fah_runapp.dart, `saved` is re-synced after sanctioned settings-hub writes (`onUserConfigFileChanged`). /// shape, flag, provider, config section, and REPL command the CLI actually
/// supports. Plain grep-friendly text (like git help); kept in pure Dart so

library;

/// header line.
String cliHelpText(String version) =>
    '''
fa — flutter_agent_harness CLI agent v$version${_buildFilterNote()}

USAGE
  fa [options]                          interactive REPL
  fa [options] "fix the tests"          headless: run one prompt and exit
  fa [options] -p "fix the tests"       headless, prompt used verbatim
  fa [options] --prompt-file p.md       headless, prompt read from a file
  fa [options] notes.md "summarize"     headless, existing file as prompt source

INVOCATION
  Interactive REPL: no prompt arguments. Type a message to run the agent;
  /commands manage the session (see REPL COMMANDS below). While a run is
  streaming, typed input steers the agent; Ctrl-C aborts the run, Ctrl-C
  while idle exits.

  Headless mode: a prompt via positional arguments (joined with spaces) or
  -p/--prompt runs a single non-interactive prompt and exits. The response
  streams to stdout; tool indicators and notices go to stderr (stdout stays
  pipeable). Nothing is ever prompted interactively — approval/ask prompts
  are denied per the non-interactive rule. The session persists like a
  normal REPL turn (including auto-compaction). Exit codes: 0 ok,
  1 provider error, 130 aborted (Ctrl-C).

  File-as-prompt: a first positional naming an EXISTING file is the prompt

  exist is treated as plain prompt text. -p text is always used verbatim

## Development Mode: Plan (plan-mode protocol appendix)

This leg runs in **plan mode**: work through an explicit, committed task
plan instead of free-form execution. Everything else in the instruction
pack still applies unchanged — this appendix only structures HOW you work.
`<KEY>` below is the current ticket key.

### 1. Decompose before editing

- Before writing any production code, break the ticket into numbered tasks
  `T1..Tn` in `outputs/<KEY>/plan.md` (the working copy).
- Every task carries exactly two fields:
  - `what` — the concrete change this task makes;
  - `verify` — how to check it passed (the command to run and the expected
    result).
- End the plan with two sections:
  - `## Decisions` — the chosen approach for every open point;
  - `## Open questions` — anything unresolved, with the workaround you picked.

### 2. Mirror the plan into a committed snapshot

- Mirror the plan to `.dmtools/plan-snapshot.md` and commit it on the dev
  branch right away: commit subject `<KEY>: plan`.
- The snapshot — not the working copy — is the durable artifact: it survives
  interruption windows and CI session-cache loss. (`outputs/` never rides
  commits.)
- When a task completes: mark its checkbox `[x]` in BOTH files and commit
  the snapshot update: `<KEY>: plan update T# done` (one commit per task).
- The periodic WIP auto-save commits keep running as usual; your plan
  commits coexist with them.

### 3. Resume rule (continuation legs)

- At leg start: if a plan file (`outputs/<KEY>/plan.md` or
  `.dmtools/plan-snapshot.md`) already exists, or the branch already carries
  commits, this leg is a CONTINUATION, not a fresh start:
  1. Read the plan and `git log`.
  2. Reconcile the plan checkboxes against the actual branch diff — a task
     whose change is already on the branch is done, checkbox or not.
  3. Execute ONLY the still-pending tasks.

### 4. Close out — the plan file never rides the pull request

- When the LAST task is done (every checkbox `[x]`), remove the snapshot
  from the branch again: `git rm .dmtools/plan-snapshot.md`, commit
  subject `<KEY>: plan done`.
- Do this BEFORE writing `outputs/<KEY>/response.md`: the completion
  report is the leg's deliverable — the plan file is leg scaffolding.
- The engine repeats this cleanup defensively before the PR is created,
  so an open pull request never carries the plan file.

**Scope estimate**: This is a moderately complex, behavior-critical persistence change in the config layer: new saveCliConfig semantics (three-way merge), project-file targeting with section upsert, a new CLI flag, plus help doc + tests. Risk: medium-high (config persistence is used by every boot; regressions clobber user configs). I estimate sp=5. Threshold 3 → plan mode. I already read the plan appendix.

**Plan tasks:**

- T1: Three-way merge core in `saveCliConfig` — new optional `base` param. RED: test that a save with `base` where a section is unchanged keeps the disk's newer value for that section while writing the changed one. GREEN: implement `_dropUnchangedTopLevelBlocks` + generalized `_preserveDiskSections`.
- T2: Removal semantics: process changed a section to absent → section is removed from disk even with the generalized backstop (models: removal case with base). RED test first.
- T3: Project targeting — `projectDir` param: changed project-capable section living in the project file is upserted there (other sections of the project file byte-preserved) and NOT written to the global file. RED tests: (a) cube change with project file carrying cube → project updated, global untouched; (b) tools change with project carrying tools → project updated; (c) section NOT in project file → still global; (d) unrelated project file content preserved byte-identically; (e) non-project section (mode) still goes global even when project file exists; multi-key combos.
- T4: `--global` flag — CliArgs boolean, wired through persistConfig call as forceGlobal. RED: parse test (`fa --global` → flag true; absent → false); saveCliConfig test: forceGlobal writes project-capable section to global even when the project file carries it.
- T5: Wire persistConfig (bin/fah_runapp.dart): pass `base: saved`, `projectDir: cliEnv.cwd`, `forceGlobal: parsed.forceGlobalConfig`. Also help text + help test entry.
- T6: Full `dart test` of touched areas + analyze + format; run the broader config/cli test files.

One more design point: the boot's own `persistConfig()` call at line 2110 — with base == saved right after load, saved.copyWith(overlays) may differ from saved at boot (mode: cli.currentMode.name — the live mode could differ from saved.mode if folder state or flags changed it... `cli.currentMode` at boot reflects effective mode which may come from `--mode` flag or folder state?). At the boot call, sections that DID change (mode from flag) get written; unchanged ones preserve disk. That's exactly right — the boot save stops re-rendering stale values.

Hmm — but careful with one thing: `mode: cli.currentMode.name` — at boot with no flag, currentMode == saved.mode → unchanged → dropped → disk preserved. With `--mode architect` → differs → written. Good.

And `allowedTools: cli.approval.alwaysAllowedTools` — boot: saved.allowedTools presumably → unchanged. Good.

`skillsAccess: skillsAccess` — a local var set from saved.skillsAccess (line 1987: `skillsAccess: saved.skillsAccess`) → unchanged. Good.

`modelRoles: cli.config.modelRolesResolver?.config ?? saved.modelRoles` — the resolver's config: built from saved roles at boot → same? The resolver might normalize/merge. If resolver normalizes differently from the raw parse, base render vs current render could differ spuriously → spurious "changed" → re-render same value → harmless (value identical, just canonicalized). Only matters when values genuinely differ.

# gh-242 plan — REPL persistConfig three-way merge

Ticket: every fa REPL rewrites the whole `~/.fah/config.yaml` from the config
it loaded at boot (`persistConfig` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`); with several
long-lived REPLs the last saver silently reverts roles/providers/keys edited
meanwhile. Plan from the ticket: three-way merge on save (only keys this
process changed vs its loaded baseline are written over the current disk
state); write to project `.fah/config.yaml` when the section lives there; add
a `--global` flag to force the global file.

## Tasks

- [ ] **T1 — three-way merge core in `saveCliConfig`** (RED first).
  New optional `base` parameter. When present, saveCliConfig renders base and
  the to-save config, splits both into top-level yaml blocks (reuse
  `_topLevelYamlBlockOf` semantics), and drops every block that is
  byte-identical between the two renders (unchanged by this process) from the
  emitted yaml; `_preserveDiskSections` generalizes (base-mode only) to
  re-attach every on-disk top-level block the emit lacks.
  - what: `lib/src/cli/cli_config.dart` — `saveCliConfig(..., {CliConfig? base})`,
    `_topLevelBlocksOf`, `_dropUnchangedBlocks`, generalized backstop.
  - verify: `dart test test/cli/cli_config_merge_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_test.dart`
    with new RED tests: stale-baseline save keeps another process's fresh
    `mode:` while writing this process's `approvalMode:`; unchanged save stays a
    no-op; legacy call shape (no base) behaves byte-identically to today.

- [ ] **T2 — removal semantics under the merge** (RED first).
  A section this process REMOVED (present in base, absent in the to-save
  render) must be deleted from disk, never resurrected by the generalized
  backstop (the `models:` empty-render removal case).
  - what: the merge returns the "removed keys" set; the backstop skips them.
  - verify: new test — base carries `models:`, save drops it → gone from disk;
    unrelated disk sections survive.

- [ ] **T3 — project-file targeting** (RED first).
  New `projectDir` parameter. Project-capable sections (`memory`, `cube`,
  `tools`, `spills`, `compaction`, `trajectory`, `logging`) that this process
  CHANGED and that LIVE in `<projectDir>/.fah/config.yaml` are upserted there
  (surgical top-level block replace; the rest of the project file stays
  byte-identical; parse-validated before the write; atomic tmp+rename,
  serialized per path) and are NOT written to the global file. Sections not
  living in the project file keep landing in the global file (legacy).
  - what: `saveCliConfig(..., {String? projectDir})` + `_saveProjectSection`
    block upsert helper.
  - verify: new tests — cube change with project file carrying `cube:` lands in
    the project file only; tools change ditto; `mode:` (user-only section)
    still lands global even when a project file exists; project file without
    the section → global write unchanged; unrelated project file content
    survives byte-for-byte; unparseable project file refuses loudly.

- [ ] **T4 — `--global` flag** (RED first).
  Boolean boot flag in `parseCliArgs` (`--global`, `_applyBooleanFlag`), doc
  line in `cli_help.dart` OPTIONS, help-test mention. Threaded into
  `saveCliConfig` as `forceGlobal`: project-capable sections land in the
  global file even when the project file carries them.
  - what: `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart` (`globalConfigSave`… final name:
    `forceGlobalConfig`), `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart`, `test/cli/cli_help_test.dart`.
  - verify: parse test (`fa --global -p x` → flag true; default false; help
    mentions it) + save test (`forceGlobal: true` writes the section to the
    global file, project file untouched).

- [ ] **T5 — wire persistConfig** (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`).
  `persistConfig` passes `base: saved` (read at call time — the
  `onUserConfigFileChanged` re-sync keeps it fresh), `projectDir: cliEnv.cwd`,
  `forceGlobal: parsed.forceGlobalConfig`.
  - what: the `persistConfig = () async { ... }` closure only.
  - verify: `dart analyze bin/fah_runapp.dart` clean; full config/cli test
    sweep green.

- [ ] **T6 — full verification**.
  `dart format` on touched files, `dart analyze` clean, run the touched test
  files + `test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart` + parity sweep
  if args are pinned there.
  - verify: commands green (see How to verify in response.md).

## Decisions

- **Section granularity**: the three-way merge compares top-level yaml blocks.
  Concurrent edits to DIFFERENT sections never clobber each other; concurrent
  edits to the SAME section stay last-writer-wins (standard, matches
  customProviders' existing per-entry-union exception which is kept as-is).
  Per-field merging inside nested sections is out of scope.
- **Baseline = the current `saved` snapshot**, read at save time inside the
  closure — the gh-1572 `onUserConfigFileChanged` re-sync keeps it equal to
  disk after sanctioned settings-hub writes, so unchanged keys keep disk truth
  across those writes too.
- **Project-capable set for saves**: `memory/cube/tools/spills/compaction/
  trajectory/logging` — the sections `cli_config.dart`'s `loadProject*`
  loaders actually read. `agent` is excluded (only `contextWindowCap` is read
  from the project file; a whole-section write would drag user-file-only keys

  not-carrying → global write, matching the existing refuse-to-clobber rules).

  (it forces the global file for session config saves; `fa config set
  --global` is an unrelated existing surface).

  behaves exactly as today (fixed `_diskPreservedSections` backstop) — only
  the boot's persistConfig opts into the merge.

content.thinking:
Progress but several failures:

1. **tools test**: my expectation is wrong — the typed render nests `mcp:` (`mcp:\n   fs: true`), not `mcp:fs: true`. Fix the test to check the nested form.

2. **"project dir == home" TIMEOUT**: DEADLOCK! `saveCliConfig` calls `saveChangedProjectSections` INSIDE `_serializedConfigWrite(file.path, ...)` for the GLOBAL file — and when projectPath == globalPath, `saveChangedProjectSections` awaits `_serializedConfigWrite(file.path, ...)` — the SAME key → waits on a chain that waits for ITSELF → deadlock. I need to:
  a. Skip targeting when the project path == global path (normalize compare) — the case my test exercises. AND
  b. Move the project write OUT of the global write's serialized op (call it before `_serializedConfigWrite(file.path, ...)` in saveCliConfig). Actually calling it inside is also wrong for the general case? No — different path keys queue fine; same path deadlocks. Safer: call the project targeting BEFORE entering the global serialized op. That also avoids nesting chains. But ordering: project write then global write — two chains could interleave with other writers... acceptable.

Let me see the other 5 failures — need full output.

arguments.content:
### What changed
- REPL `persistConfig` no longer rewrites the whole `~/.fah/config.yaml` from its boot snapshot: `saveCliConfig` takes the loaded baseline and renders only the sections this process changed over the current disk state (three-way merge per top-level yaml block).
- Changed project-capable sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`/`spills`/`compaction`/`trajectory`/`logging`) that live in `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` are written THERE (surgical block upsert, parse-validated, atomic) instead of the global file; removals never touch the project file.
- New `--global` boot flag forces the global file for every section.

### Key decisions
- Baseline is the executable's `saved` snapshot read at save time — the existing `onUserConfigFileChanged` re-sync keeps it equal to disk after sanctioned settings-hub writes.
- Section granularity: concurrent edits to different sections never clobber each other; same-section edits stay last-writer-wins (matches the existing `customProviders` union exception).
- No baseline (`base == null`) keeps the legacy caller-wins whole-save contract byte-for-byte; only the boot's `persistConfig` opts in (`base`/`projectDir`/`forceGlobal`).
- Merge machinery lives in a `part` file (`lib/src/cli/config_save_merge.dart`) — no new public barrel surface.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli_config_three_way_test.dart test/cli/cli_config_merge_test.dart \
  test/cli/cli_config_test.dart test/cli/config_section_preservation_reg_test.dart
dart run bin/fa.dart --help | grep -- '--global'
```

<details><summary>Save flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[persistConfig: saved.copyWith overlays] --> M[three-way merge vs baseline]
  M -->|section unchanged| K[drop from emit - disk block survives]
  M -->|section changed| E[render block]
  E -->|project-capable + lives in project file| P[upsert into project file]
  E -->|otherwise| G[global emit]
  K --> W[global write: emit + re-attached disk blocks]
  P --> W
```
</details>

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR

    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then

    fi

stage_coverage() {
  if [ ! -d coverage ]; then
    echo "❌ coverage/ not found — run the test-core stage first" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "📊 Formatting coverage to lcov..."
  dart run coverage:format_coverage --lcov -i coverage -o coverage/lcov.info
  echo "🔍 Checking line coverage (baseline: >= ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)..."
  if ! python3 scripts/check_coverage.py "$COVERAGE_BASELINE"; then
    echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — TEST COVERAGE (baseline ${COVERAGE_BASELINE}%)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

stage_crap() {
  if ! command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 2  # caller prints SKIP marker
  fi
  # gh-1738: version floor BEFORE running anything — the root config's
  # gates.similarity block ConfigExceptions on <0.15.0 parsers, which
  # would surface here mislabeled as "CRAP RATCHET FAILED".
  local c4d_ver
  c4d_ver=$(dart pub global list 2>/dev/null | awk '$1=="crap4dart"{print $2}')
  case "$c4d_ver" in
    0.1[5-9].*|0.[2-9][0-9].*|[1-9].*) ;;
    "")
      return 2  # not activated — caller prints SKIP marker
      ;;
    *)
      echo "⚠️  crap4dart $c4d_ver is too old for this tree (need >= 0.15.0 —" \
           "gh-1738 similarity keys); skipping — run: dart pub global activate" \
           "crap4dart '>=0.15.0 <0.16.0'" >&2
      return 2  # caller prints SKIP marker
      ;;
  esac
  if dart pub global run crap4dart --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "🔍 Checking CRAP scores (ratchet pinned in crap4dart.yaml)..."
    # Reuses the fresh coverage/lcov.info produced by the coverage stage.
    # Hook mode scopes the analysis to the STAGED lib/bin files: the
    # ratchet guards what a commit touches, so a pre-existing offender in
    # an untouched file cannot block an unrelated commit. CI keeps the
    # whole-repo analyze, so nothing escapes the ratchet permanently.
    local files=""
    if [ "$HOOK_MODE" -eq 1 ]; then
      files=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM \
        | grep -E '^(lib|bin)/.*\.dart$' || true)
      if [ -z "$files" ]; then
        echo "   no staged lib/bin sources — nothing to ratchet"
        return 0
      fi
      echo "   hook scope: $(echo "$files" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') staged file(s)"
      if ! dart pub global run crap4dart analyze $files; then
        echo "❌ QUALITY GATE FAILED — CRAP RATCHET" >&2
        exit 1
      fi

## gh-2422 — REPL persistConfig overwrites config.yaml from stale boot state

**Done.** Branch `ai/gh-2422`, 7 commits past `origin/main`, tree clean, all tests green.

### What changed
- `saveCliConfig` gained a `base` (boot-baseline) parameter: the save renders only the top-level sections this process actually changed vs the baseline over the current disk state; a generalized backstop re-attaches every on-disk block the emit lacks (removed sections stay removed). The REPL's `persistConfig` passes its `saved` snapshot as the baseline, so a long-lived REPL can no longer re-render boot values over another process's mid-session edits.
- Changed project-capable sections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`/`spills`/`compaction`/`trajectory`/`logging`) that live in `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` are written THERE (surgical block upsert, parse-validated, atomic, other lines byte-identical) instead of the global file; the global copy stays untouched. Removals never delete a project section (repo-traveling policy is not the session's to delete).
- New `--global` boot flag (`forceGlobalConfig` in CliArgs) forces the global file for every section; documented in `fa --help` and the help-sync test.

### Key decisions
- Section-granularity merge; same-section concurrency stays last-writer-wins (matches the existing `customProviders` union exception, kept as-is).
- No baseline (`base == null`) keeps the legacy caller-wins whole-save contract byte-for-byte — only the boot's persistConfig opts in.
- Merge machinery lives in a `part` file (`lib/src/cli/config_save_merge.dart`, 268 lines) — no new public barrel surface; `cli_config.dart` stays at 2492 lines (< 2800 gate).
- Project targeting runs outside the global write chain (a workspace whose project file IS the global file would otherwise deadlock on the same chain key).

### Verification
- Full deterministic suite: **15,365 passed / 16 skipped** (live-macOS legs), exit 0 (`dart test --exclude-tags integration,llm,browser-ext,perf,pty`).
- Fresh post-refactor focused sweep: 797 passed (config/args/help/settings/tools/cube/models/quota/parity); self-config integration leg: 3 passed.
- Scoped lcov on the new file: 95.8% lines (4 misses = defensive/unreachable-by-contract branches); max CRAP 10.02 < 12; `dart analyze lib bin test` clean; `dart format` clean.
- End-to-end smoke: 3 real headless runs against a sandboxed HOME — the global config stayed byte-identical (boot save is a no-op under the merge); `fa --help` renders the flag.

- Integration readiness: no concerns — the feature is pure local file logic, no external setup required. `outputs/concerns.md` intentionally not written.

<details><summary>Save flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S[persistConfig: saved.copyWith overlays] --> M[three-way merge vs baseline]
  M -->|section unchanged| K[drop from emit - disk block survives]
  M -->|section changed| E[render block]
  E -->|project-capable and lives in project file| P[upsert into project file]
  E -->|otherwise| G[global emit]
  K --> W[global write: emit + re-attached disk blocks]
  P --> W
```
</details>
